title: ACT-AGE
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: High schooler Kei Yonagi is raising her two younger siblings after their father left and their mother died, and she dreams of acting. Her method acting draws so deeply on her own memories that she can lose track of reality, and director Sumiji Kuroyama takes her on to develop that dangerous talent through film and stage productions. The series ended abruptly in August 2020 after the writer's arrest, and later volumes were cancelled in Japan and English (Wikipedia, citing Anime News Network and NHK; ComicBook.com).
life_message: It holds up pouring your whole self into your art, while asking what that costs and who keeps you grounded.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kei proves herself through auditions and performances, not personal confrontation.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Kei's unconventional method breaks industry norms, and the story backs her freedom to act her way.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Her motivation is providing for her siblings; family comes first.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Director-protege mentorship and rival agency structures, but talent outranks seniority.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Craft and technique, not custom or religion, guide the characters.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Despite poverty, the story centers self-expression through art.

folkways.japan: The talent-agency system, entertainment-industry hierarchy and a teenager carrying household duties reflect Japanese show-business and family settings.

delivery.evidence: No review comment on delivery found; summaries show the cost of immersive acting through Kei's productions (to verify).
delivery.note: Summaries show the story weighing artistic immersion against its cost through Kei's roles and her mentor's guidance.

winners_losers: Raw, self-taught talent and the mentors who protect it win; manufactured celebrity is questioned. The story sympathizes with Kei's artistic hunger while showing its danger.
